title: Design System: Clank landing and builder board

display.purpose: Compact landing heading; 36px at the narrow breakpoint.

body.purpose: Base type inherited by builder content and controls.

prompt.purpose: Bare prompt textarea within the project-tab composer.

code.purpose: Local commands and disclosed tool output.

demo-title.purpose: Browser-demo introduction; 20px at the narrow breakpoint.

shadows.name: demo-cursor
shadows.purpose: Local cursor separation from canvas and preview; not a surface elevation scale.

motion.name: working-indicator
motion.purpose: Progress line and thinking dot; disabled for reduced motion.

motion.name: graph-flow
motion.value: 1.2s linear infinite; stroke-dashoffset 0 → -9; working input paths .5s
motion.purpose: Directional 1/8 dotted paths. Paused offscreen or when hidden; disabled for reduced motion.

motion.name: graph-packet
motion.purpose: Active real output pulse from the submit port to its destination; hidden for reduced motion.

motion.name: demo-packet
motion.purpose: Active demo edge pulse; shares demo playback and visibility gating.

motion.name: demo-loading
motion.purpose: Preview startup indicator; paused with demo playback, offscreen, or when hidden; disabled for reduced motion.

motion.name: demo-phase-timing
motion.value: Scripted: type 900–3500ms, submit 4200ms, editing 5900ms, checks 9500ms, preview startup 10400ms, ready 11700ms, checkbox 12800ms, end 13500ms; work-step dwell: 1700ms, 1200ms, 1200ms, 1200ms, 900ms, 1300ms
motion.purpose: Reading, three file edits, checks, preview startup, and completion drive the session summary, sidebar history, and incremental diff counts. Scripted playback pauses offscreen/hidden or through Pause. Reduced motion retains discrete progression and a static cursor. Explicit Clank follow tracks the cursor; opening a session conversation preserves the camera.

motion.name: demo-progress-transitions
motion.value: session height 200ms ease; code height 240ms ease; sidebar width/height 220ms ease; counts 320ms; content 160–200ms
motion.purpose: Measured progress content, incremental file rows/counts, and sidebar expansion; all disabled or zero-duration for reduced motion.

components.name: Scripted demo browser
components.description: Browser chrome and a ready preview sample at two of four habits complete. Every prompt runs the same local habit tracker without real AI, authentication, voice, or backend work. Initial playback and Replay alone animate cursor typing, submit, and checking a third habit; Replay resets the original session and hides its outputs until their stages recur, preserves other sessions, and restarts after completed playback. The blue cursor persists during manual work and after completion, with a clickable Clank tag and Idle/Working dot; reduced motion retains a static cursor with Next step and no automatic checking. Its 25px pointer uses #8aa4ff with #dce4ff edge and a matching click pulse; the tag uses #111b3c text at 11px/600, 3px 7px padding, and a 4px radius. A circle-only blue mascot at the upper right opens a 312px sidebar beside the 414px-high canvas. At 699px and below, chat is 340px high below the 370px canvas, without overlap. The header has a compact blue @Clank native button (#b7c6ff text on #8aa4ff24, 1px 5px padding, 4px radius) with hover and keyboard focus. Its accessible name is “Follow Clank on canvas”; activation centers the cursor at the current zoom and enables follow without closing chat or interrupting playback. Sidebar Working text and its filled dot use the demo-added token; Idle stays gray. Code diff counts use demo-added and demo-removed with visible plus/minus signs. User messages are right-aligned #262626 bubbles with an 88% maximum width, 7px radius, and 7px 10px padding, without a visible “you” label; assistant messages keep the “clank” label, without avatars. Conversation and desktop input are 13px, follow-up actions 12px, mobile input 16px, and metadata 10–11px. Requests retain conversation and status and create separate example rows without moving the camera. Opening the avatar or cursor tag enables follow without interrupting scripted playback. Follow centers the cursor in the canvas excluding the sidebar at the current zoom, through completion and resize; Replay preserves following. Following Clank, user panning, node dragging, explicit focus, or new work exit follow. Show session and View preview keep the sidebar open; Close and Escape restore launcher focus. Ordinary controls remain monochrome. The companion and runtime behavior are omitted from this preview specimen. The demo graph is repository → session → worktree → preview. Repository and Fork ports create drafts from main or a parent worktree; the left worktree input creates a reuse draft, and a draft output can connect there to reuse existing code and preview. New/fork worktrees appear after submission and previews only at startup; reuse and follow-ups update existing worktrees and retain already-visible previews. Only drafts reconnect. Enter on the repository, Fork, or worktree-input port creates the corresponding draft. Lineage is retained; busy fork/reuse attempts preserve the draft with an error, and one writer can edit a worktree at a time. Blank-canvas and port creation keep the camera still, with draft textarea focus after measurement and scrolling prevented. Node selection and keyboard focus color the actual tab/body borders with demo-selection, without an offset outline or glow. Submitted session bodies open their corresponding sidebar chat; context labels remain draggable. Each session retains its own history and continues on the same worktree after completion; its composer is disabled while working. Creation and session-chat opening preserve the camera. Deletion controls are paused. Staged reading, file edits, checks, preview startup, and completion update summaries, heights, and signed diff counts; reduced motion disables the transitions. The public default is Prompt + activity. Four development-only variants remain unselected exploration. Grouping, backend work, and artifacts remain deferred.

components.name: Canvas session menu
components.description: One-action menu shared by blank board and demo panes. The board places a fresh draft without moving its viewport. The demo creates an independent draft from main at the flow coordinate, keeps the camera still, waits for node measurements before focusing its textarea with scrolling prevented, and retains existing sessions. New/fork submission creates local example output nodes; reconnecting a draft to a worktree reuses its existing outputs.

narrative.overview:
Clank uses a graphite field, white and gray controls, and the existing mascot rendered in grayscale. Compact setup controls keep the prompt central. Thin borders, restrained tonal shifts, and dotted connections organize source material without adding decorative panels.

This document covers only the landing page and builder board rendered inside `.clank-builder`, including the board's embedded sign-in and project forms. Pricing, account, onboarding, and other existing pages retain their incumbent system. Implementation evidence lives in `src/lib/builder/`, with shared font definitions in `src/app.css`; surface composition belongs in `.impeccable/landing.brief.md`.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite surfaces with white actions and neutral gray structure.
A small project tab, bare prompt field, and compact footer controls.
Directional dotted input connections on desktop and a scrolling input strip on mobile.
A static, radially faded dot field on entry and a pannable project board.
A labelled browser-frame demo with draggable nodes and a working sample preview.

rules.name: The Monochrome Builder Rule
rules.body: Use white, gray, and graphite for builder chrome, actions, and errors. Keep the Clank mascot in CSS grayscale; user images, app previews, and existing routes retain their own content colors. The demo’s Clank cursor and companion presence are the approved local blue exception, including the avatar background, @Clank header button, and chat caret. The demo also uses green for diff additions and current work labels/dots, red for diff removals, and muted orange on selected node borders. These semantic exceptions do not extend to other controls; Idle stays gray.

rules.name: The Directed Flow Rule
rules.body: Connect sources to their actual controls and move dots and active packets from source to destination. Keep the landing background still so motion explains work.

dos: Do preserve the recognizable Clank mascot in grayscale and the shared SVG icon geometry.
Do use brightness, neutral borders, and visible keyboard focus to distinguish controls and state.
Do keep project source in the tab and execution inside the prompt footer.
Do retain independent mobile scrolling for input material and the draft/authentication region.
Do retain the board's readable widget widths and narrow-screen Chat/Preview tabs.
Do anchor repository, image, and output connections to their corresponding controls and keep motion directional.
Do pause connection and demo motion offscreen or when hidden, and preserve manual progression under reduced motion.
Do keep the demo labelled as scripted and its node contents readable through panning and preview focus.
donts: Don't add pink or extend color beyond Clank presence blue, green additions/current work, red removals, and muted orange node selection in the demo.
Don't apply this scoped palette to existing pricing, account, or onboarding pages.
Don't use tiny status-label sizes as the default for operational text.
Don't let canvas dragging consume normal interaction inside forms, input material, transcripts, or previews.
Don't imply real input satellites are independent draggable nodes or that image attachments sync across browsers.
Don't present the demo’s separate working-copy and preview nodes as a change to the signed-in project widget.
